about.title: Every building in Stockholm, and when it was built
about.lead: Every building standing in Stockholm municipality today ({buildings} of them), coloured by when it was built. Play the city's growth, pick a range of years, or open any building to see what we know about it and how we know it.

about.use.period: Click a period in the legend to see it alone.
about.use.floors: Floors colours the city by how many floors each building has.

about.years.title: Where the years come from
about.years.lead: {with_year} buildings ({with_year_pct}) have a year. {record} come from a record: RAÄ's heritage register, a short hand-checked list of landmarks, Wikidata or OpenStreetMap. {area} take the year RAÄ gives their whole area, and {estimated} houses are estimated from similar dated buildings nearby. The other {unknown} have no year in any open source yet. They are drawn as “Year unknown”, and the map does not guess.
about.years.kinds: A year from a record is shown as the record gives it: an exact year ({exact} buildings), the year a building was finished when the record gives a span of up to fifteen years ({range}), or the first year of a longer span ({long}).
about.years.private: A private house (a villa, a row or chain house, or an allotment cottage) shows only its decade, never its exact year: {private_dated} of the {private_cat} private houses have one. Its colour still shows its period, so where a period begins or ends within the decade, the colour narrows the decade to the part inside that period, never to fewer than {fewest} years.
about.src.raa_old: RAÄ's older register file (years the current register dropped)
about.src.raa_area: RAÄ, for a whole area (a district or an estate)
about.src.reader: A reader's report, checked by the map's maker
about.src.estimate: Estimated from similar dated buildings nearby
about.acc.title: How the estimates work, and how good they are
about.acc.how: For a house with no year, the map looks at the most similar dated buildings nearby (where they stand, how tall and how big they are, and what kind of building they are) and takes their typical year, the closest and most similar weighing most. To test this, every dated building was estimated as if it had no year, from the others, with whole city blocks left out together.
about.acc.rule: The map shows an estimated decade (“≈ 1950s”) only when all of these hold:
about.acc.rule.house: it is a house (a villa, a row or a chain house);
about.acc.rule.near: a dated building stands within {near} m;
about.acc.rule.late: the City first mapped it before {late}, and its property unit, where known, was not formed late (such buildings are mostly new);
about.acc.rule.cell: its cell of the test has at least {min_cell} test buildings, puts at least {min_right} of them in the right period, and has a band of ±{max_band} years or less.
about.acc.result: {estimated} houses are estimated. In the test, {right} of the test houses in the cells the map uses were estimated in the right period ({right_n} of {n}), and {within} within one period. A cell's band is the range around the estimate that eight in ten true years fall inside.
about.acc.houses: The houses the map estimates, cell by cell:
about.acc.others: The other cells: houses the map does not estimate, and the other building types (the map estimates none of them)
about.acc.check: An independent check, on {check_n} buildings that only Wikidata or OpenStreetMap dates: the rule gave {check_shown} of them a decade, {check_right} in the right period. It is too small to confirm the test's figure.
about.acc.check.measured: An independent check, on {check_n} buildings that only Wikidata or OpenStreetMap dates: the rule gave {check_shown} of them a decade, {check_right} in the right period.
about.acc.check.new: It gave none of the {check_new} built from 1990 on a decade: a new building among older ones is the estimate's blind spot, and the rule keeps them off the map.
about.acc.area: Dating a building with its whole area was checked on {area_n} buildings that RAÄ dates both ways: the area's year put {area_right} of them in the right period.
about.limits.title: What the map cannot tell you
about.limits.standing: Only buildings standing today. Demolished buildings are not on the map, so Play shows when today's buildings were built, not how fast the city grew.
about.limits.snapshot: A snapshot from {snapshot}. The City's 3D model is from then: buildings finished after it are missing.
about.limits.one: One year per building. Where a record gives a span of up to fifteen years, the map shows the year the building was finished; for a longer history it shows the first year, and the card gives the span.
about.limits.gamla: Gamla stan is mostly “Year unknown”. Only {gamla_dated} of its {gamla_n} buildings have a year from a record, and the old town is not estimated, because the test shows it cannot be done well.
about.limits.new: New buildings are the estimate's blind spot: a new house among old ones would take its neighbours' age, so the map estimates no building the City first mapped in {late} or later.
about.limits.height: Heights are to the roof: spires and towers are not included. Floors come from OpenStreetMap where mapped ({floors_osm} buildings) and otherwise from the height (≈).
about.limits.colour: Colour shows the era, not the paint: a building's colour is its period, not the colour of its walls.
about.limits.private: Private houses show their decade only (see Privacy).
about.limits.terrain: The ground is drawn true to scale. The Hills slider under Look raises the hills up to {relief_max} times as high, or lays the city flat. The heights come from {terrain_from}.
about.limits.terrain.scaled: The ground is drawn {relief} times as high as it is. The Hills slider under Look sets it from flat up to {relief_max} times. The heights come from {terrain_from}.
about.limits.terrain.dtm: Lantmäteriet's terrain model (Markhöjdmodell Nedladdning, laser-scanned in 2020–2021)
about.privacy.title: Privacy
about.privacy.lead: This map is about buildings, not people.
about.privacy.shows: What the map shows. For every building in Stockholm municipality: its outline and height, the year or decade it was built and how we know it, and, where open public sources have them, its name, architect, street address, the City Museum's heritage rating, legal protection, a photo and a short text from Wikipedia.
about.privacy.never.who: Who owns or lives in a building: sentences in the Wikipedia texts that say so are left out.
about.privacy.never.ids: Property designations (fastighetsbeteckningar) or the registers' internal building and property ids.
about.privacy.never.byggherre: Who had a building built (the byggherre), except where the building's own name carries it, as many old names do.
about.privacy.never.year: The exact year of a private house.
about.privacy.private: Private houses. Villas, row and chain houses and allotment cottages show only the decade they were built, for example “1950s”, never the exact year, and their cards do not link to the heritage register's record. An architect's name is left off a private house when it appears on {rare} or fewer buildings in the whole city, because on a family home a rare name may belong to the owner. Names of firms and housing cooperatives still show. Links to Wikipedia and Wikidata, Wikipedia texts and photos are left off private houses too, unless the house is one of the hand-checked landmarks.
about.privacy.private.address: A private house's street address is not shown on its card either, and search does not find it by its address.
about.privacy.why: Why we may show this. Everything comes from open public sources (see Sources). We publish it because we have a legitimate interest in telling the story of how Stockholm was built (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)). To keep that interest from outweighing anyone's privacy, we limit what is shown about private homes as described above.
about.privacy.visit: Your visit. The map sets no cookies and runs no analytics or tracking script. The site is hosted by Cloudflare, which handles the technical details of each request, such as your IP address and browser, to deliver and protect the site. We look only at overall figures, such as the number of visits and the countries they come from. The map remembers your choices (look, hills, language, the legend and its switches) in your own browser; they are never sent to us. Photos are copied to this site, so opening a card contacts no other service. Links to RAÄ, Wikipedia, Wikidata and OpenStreetMap open their own sites, which have their own privacy policies.
about.privacy.form: The report form. If you use “Something wrong?” on a card or “Suggest something” under Contact, we store what you send: your message, your email address, the reference of the building the card shows and, if you add one, your photo and the name to credit it with. We use it only to answer you and to fix the map. Your IP address is not stored: to stop abuse, the site counts reports from each connection for an hour by a scrambled code it cannot trace back, then forgets it. We delete your email address twelve months after your report is closed. A photo is used under the licence you grant (CC BY 4.0, credited with the name you give). Nothing we publish from a report, such as an issue on the project's GitHub, includes your email address. The form sets no cookies.
about.privacy.hide: Hide a building, or correct it. If you own or live in a building and want its details taken off the map, or you have found a mistake, use “Something wrong?” on its card or write to {contact}. You do not need to say why. A hidden building keeps its shape, but its year, name, architect, address and links are removed in the next data update, as soon as we can and within the time the GDPR sets. You can also complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY).
about.privacy.hide.nocontact: Hide a building, or correct it. If you own or live in a building and want its details taken off the map, or you have found a mistake, the address to write to is published under Contact before the map goes public. You will not need to say why. A hidden building keeps its shape, but its year, name, architect, address and links are removed in the next data update, as soon as we can and within the time the GDPR sets. You can also complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY).
about.privacy.who: Who is responsible. Hus för hus is a non-commercial project by {maker}, the controller of this data under the GDPR. The data is kept as long as the map is online and is replaced with every data update.
about.privacy.who.nomaker: Who is responsible. Hus för hus is a non-commercial project; its maker is named under Contact before the map goes public. The data is kept as long as the map is online and is replaced with every data update.

about.sources.odbl: The map's building database (its tiles, cards and search files) contains information from OpenStreetMap and is published under the Open Database License (ODbL 1.0) as a whole; each source above keeps its own credit.
about.thanks.title: Thanks
about.thanks.code: Built on {amsterdam} by Alex Barakov (MIT licence), and inspired by Sasha Bogachev's {paris}, which gave the idea of terrain, a range of years and search (no code from it is used).
about.thanks.more: Also three.js (MIT licence); the fonts Albert Sans, Familjen Grotesk, Inter and Schibsted Grotesk (SIL Open Font License, the licence files beside them); the RAÄ, OpenStreetMap and Wikidata communities; and Stadsmuseet, whose classification RAÄ publishes.
